terms.description: The main antagonist defeated by the party, signifying the end of a major conflict.
One of Frieren's former companions, known as 'The Hero'. He seems focused on his appearance (handsome looks). Research confirms he is the main hero, male.
One of Frieren's former companions, identified as a Warrior. Context implies he is a Dwarf.
One of Frieren's former companions, identified as a Priest. Often hungover and enjoys drinking.
The protagonist, an Elf Mage. Her perspective dominates the narrative timeline.
A very small amount of money (ten coins) given as payment or reward by the king.
A creature or monster that typically disguises itself as an inanimate object, mentioned as attempting to eat Frieren.
A general term for reanimated corpses or beings returned from death, used here metaphorically to describe Heiter's pallor.
A celestial event occurring every fifty years, chosen as a significant marker for the start of the new age of peace.
An object looted from the Demon King's castle, possessing an evil aura, which Frieren needs for a summoning spell.
Eisen's race, implied by Frieren's comment that he hasn't changed much, as expected from a Dwarf.
Heiter's later title/rank within the church, indicating advancement from his former role as a Priest.
The location where Heiter serves as a Bishop.
A historical figure whose tomb yielded a grimoire containing potential resurrection/immortality spells.
A magical book, specifically one unearthed from Ewig the Sage's tomb, written in code using pictures.
A deity whom Heiter jokingly suggests might not forgive him for his past behavior.
The spiritual or magical energy source used by mages, central to casting spells.
Fern's background; she lost her parents during a war in the southern lands.
The region where Fern originated as a war orphan.
The general area Frieren plans to travel across for the next hundred years collecting spells.
Pests mentioned by Fern that consume seeds, which she initially intends to release in the woods.
A specific type of flower that grows in Frieren's homeland and Himmel's hometown; Frieren obsessively searches for it to learn a conjuring spell.
The profession or role of an unnamed woman who assists Frieren and Fern with local flora.
Simple, everyday spells acquired as payment, such as one that produces warm tea.
Himmel's favorite food, which Frieren recalled when trying to name her favorite food.
The specific dessert Fern chooses at the restaurant, which Frieren somehow knew in advance.
The Elder Sage of Corruption, a powerful demon mage sealed away eighty years ago by Himmel's party. He created the spell Zoltraak.
The name of the historically famous 'killing magic' developed by Qual, designed to pierce defenses and destroy the body directly. It has since been integrated into general human magic.
The legendary mage considered the founder of humanity's magic. Books attributed to her are generally considered forgeries.
The land where souls are said to rest, mentioned in connection with a grimoire by Flamme.
A village festival where it is customary to watch the first sunrise of the new year from the seashore, which the villagers clean in preparation for the event.

The concept of an afterlife where souls are believed to go. Its existence is debated by the characters, with Heiter advocating for it as a 'convenient' belief. It is equated with Aureole in Flamme's notes.
A geographical area where Frieren and Fern search for and discover the genuine notes of Flamme the Legendary Mage, hidden near a large tree over some ruins.
The northernmost region of the continent, where the Demon King's castle is located. It is the destination for Frieren's new journey to find Aureole.
A region that must be traveled through to reach Ende, located on the path Himmel's party originally took.
A canyon that must be crossed to reach the northern lands. Eisen's apprentice, Stark, is found in a village near it.
A crafty monster that consumes only humans. It uses powerful illusion magic to create phantoms of its victims' deceased loved ones to lure them in.
A powerful type of dragon that is very tough and a fast flyer. It builds its nest using objects infused with magic, including a grimoire that Frieren wishes to acquire.

A young warrior and Eisen's apprentice. Despite his immense talent, he is extremely cowardly, having fled a monster attack on his hometown. He is recruited by Frieren and Fern as their party's front-liner.
A male demon who is one of Aura the Guillotine's executioners. He uses magical wire to decapitate his victims and attacks Frieren in her prison cell.
A group of the most powerful demons directly serving the Demon King. Aura the Guillotine is one of its members.
The ruler (Count) of the northern town where Frieren is imprisoned. He is negotiating with demons who have presented themselves as peace envoys.
A male demon serving under Aura the Guillotine. He acts as the chief negotiator of the supposed "peace envoys" and is exceptionally powerful and intimidating.
A female demon serving under Aura the Guillotine, part of the "peace envoy" group. She is noted to be skilled at locating magic.
The substance that demons dissolve into upon death. Since they leave no corpse, their transformation into these particles is the only proof of their demise.

context_guide: The tone of 'Frieren' (Sousou no Frieren) is predominantly melancholic, reflective, and philosophical, focusing on themes of time, mortality, memory, and the meaning of human connection as experienced by an immortal elf. The style mixes high fantasy adventure tropes (dungeons, magic) with slice-of-life moments and deep emotional resonance. The world is post-heroic, dealing with the aftermath of a great victory. Translations must capture the somber, respectful, and ancient nature of Frieren's dialogue, contrasted with the more energetic or straightforward speech of her human companions. Honorifics (like -san, -chan) are crucial for conveying social dynamics and should be noted, although direct Greek equivalents might be adapted contextually.
